articles.title: Jornalista Antônio Carlos De Júlio morre aos 81 anos em Campinas | G1
articles.standfirst: Referência na imprensa, De Júlio acumulou passagens pela EPTV e TVB/SBT, chefiou a editoria de Esportes do Correio Popular e atuou na assessoria do Guarani, entre outros.
articles.summary: Referência na imprensa, De Júlio acumulou passagens pela EPTV e TVB/SBT, chefiou a editoria de Esportes do Correio Popular e atuou na assessoria do Guarani, entre outros.
articles.body:
O jornalista Antônio Carlos De Júlio morreu aos 81 anos nesta quarta-feira (11), em Campinas (SP) — Foto: Reprodução

O jornalista Antônio Carlos De Júlio morreu aos 81 anos nesta quarta-feira (11), em Campinas (SP). A causa da morte não foi informada.

Referência na imprensa campineira, acumulou passagens pela EPTV Campinas na década de 1980, atuou na TVB/SBT, chefiou a editoria de Esportes do Correio Popular, foi correspondente de O Estado de S. Paulo e trabalhou na assessoria do Guarani Futebol Clube, entre outros.

"Neste momento de luto, a Prefeitura de Campinas presta homenagem à sua trajetória e manifesta solidariedade aos familiares, amigos e colegas de profissão", destacou a administração, em nota.

Já o Guarani publicou nota em que "expressa sua solidariedade aos familiares, amigos e colegas de profissão, desejando força e conforto neste momento de luto".

O velório de Antônio Carlos De Júlio será realizado nesta quinta-feira (12), a partir das 8h, no Cemitério da Saudade, em Campinas. O sepultamento está previsto para as 11h.

articles.title: La FIFA examina en Madrid dos pilares de la candidatura al Mundial 2030
articles.standfirst: Inspeccionarán dos de los grandes escenarios de la candidatura, el Santiago Bernabéu y el Riyadh Air Metropolitano
articles.summary: Inspeccionarán dos de los grandes escenarios de la candidatura, el Santiago Bernabéu y el Riyadh Air Metropolitano
articles.body: La candidatura española para el Mundial 2030 marca la agenda de Rafael Louzán. Mientras la selección disputa este jueves en Praga su quinto partido de la fase de grupos de la Nations League ante la República Checa (20.45 horas), el presidente de la RFEF ha permanecido en Madrid para atender uno de los asuntos estratégicos más importantes del fútbol español: la visita de inspección de la delegación de la FIFA a las sedes candidatas. Los representantes del organismo internacional llegaron este miércoles por la noche a la capital después de completar su etapa en Zaragoza. Durante su estancia en Madrid inspeccionarán los dos grandes escenarios de la candidatura, el Santiago Bernabéu y el Riyadh Air Metropolitano, antes de continuar su recorrido por otras ciudades aspirantes. Louzán mantendrá este jueves una reunión de trabajo con la delegación de la FIFA para analizar las visitas realizadas hasta el momento y coordinar los siguientes pasos del proceso. Un encuentro considerado prioritario dentro de la hoja de ruta hacia el Mundial de 2030 y que explica su ausencia junto a la expedición de la selección en la República Checa. La ronda de inspecciones arrancó en San Sebastián y Bilbao, continuó en Barcelona, con visitas al Spotify Camp Nou y al RCDE Stadium, y posteriormente hizo escala en Zaragoza para conocer el proyecto de la Nueva Romareda. Tras Madrid, la delegación viajará a Sevilla y Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, mientras que las evaluaciones de Valencia y Vigo han quedado fijadas para el mes de diciembre. La importancia de esta fase de análisis técnico, centrada en estadios, accesos e infraestructuras, ha llevado a Louzán a quedarse en España en una semana con doble compromiso para la selección. El presidente federativo no estará en Praga, pero sí tiene previsto acudir el próximo domingo al Metropolitano para presenciar el choque entre España e Inglaterra, último partido del equipo de Luis de la Fuente en este parón internacional.

images.caption: Louzán, junto a Infantino durante el Mundial, en Atlanta. RFEF

articles.title: Pep Guardiola Reportedly 'Top Target' for USMNT amid Mauricio Pochettino, Manchester United Rumors
articles.summary: U.S. Soccer intends to take a big swing in the event coach Mauricio Pochettino takes the Manchester United job.
articles.body:
U.S. Soccer intends to take a big swing in the event coach Mauricio Pochettino takes the Manchester United job.

The Athletic's Paul Tenorio, Henry Bushnell and Tom Bogert reported former Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola would be "a top target" in the coaching search.

"Guardiola has had dialogue with U.S. Soccer in the past, and has long been intrigued by the prospect of working in America," the report said.

Pochettino's move to Manchester United isn't yet official, but the Guardian 's Jamie Jackson reported the sides have struck "a framework agreement."

If U.S. Soccer's objective is replacing Pochettino with a world-class manager, then Guardiola would absolutely fit the bill. He collected a bevy of trophies during his stints at Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Manchester City.

As great as Guardiola's track record is, however, appointing him to a national team might be a bit of a risk.

The 55-year-old is obsessive about details big and small when it comes to his squads. As a national team coach, he wouldn't have anywhere near as much time to work with his players in training.

If anything, Guardiola attempting to carry over his usual practices could backfire. The players would be overwhelmed with information and suggestions about how to fulfill his tactical vision.

For U.S. Soccer, the solution may not be as simple as bringing Guardiola aboard and ending the process there, either.

It's not a coincidence that his longest individual spell came at a club that built itself completely in his image.

Manchester City laid the foundation for Guardiola's arrival when it hired two notable figures with Barcelona ties, Txiki Begiristain and Ferran Soriano, in 2012. Guardiola was supported in every way across his decade there.

Contrast that to his time at Barca and Bayern. Barcelona's internal politics were eventually too much for even him , and he was never truly beloved at Bayern because he couldn't deliver the Champions League title everyone in Bavaria coveted.

For U.S. Soccer, the logic is obvious. A tactician as good as Guardiola should help the men's national team reach a level it has never reached before.

Still, this may not be the home run hire a lot of people will immediately expect if it comes together.

articles.title: Zidane confirma la ausencia de Mbappé contra Italia
articles.standfirst: El atacante del Real Madrid sufre unas molestias en el bíceps femoral... pero continúa en la concentración de Francia
articles.summary: El atacante del Real Madrid sufre unas molestias en el bíceps femoral... pero continúa en la concentración de Francia
articles.body: Era un secreto a voces y, después de las alarmas que se han encendido esta mañana, sólo faltaba la confirmación oficial: Kylian Mbappé no jugará mañana contra Italia tras sufrir unas molestias en el bíceps femoral. "Kylian no estará disponible mañana. Sintió una leve molestia", informó Zinedine Zidane en la previa del encuentro contra Italia que se disputa mañana en San Siro. "Como siempre, no hay ningún riesgo. Estas cosas son lamentables, pero son parte del juego. Espero que podamos contar con él el domingo". Por tanto, a diferencia de lo sucedido con Kalulu, Tchouaméni y Marcus Thuram, Mbappé no regresará a Madrid y continuará en la concentración de la selección francesa... con la esperanza de poder tener minutos en el último partido del grupo contra Turquía, agendado para el próximo domingo (20.45h) en Lyon. "Creo que está bien. La prueba es que se queda con nosotros. No está contento, le hubiera gustado jugar mañana. No debemos correr riesgos porque la temporada es larga", se encargó de reiterar un Zinedine Zidane que deberá recomponer su frente de ataque. En principio, parece que será Barcola quien ejerza de '9' por delante de Olise, Cherki y Doué. Kroupi, recordemos, fue citado ayer por la baja de Thuram... mientras que Mayulu se ha incorporado a última hora. "Yo selecciono a los jugadores y a veces las cosas pasan. En noviembre, con la liga y la Champions League, hay que aceptarlo. Es lamentable. Como entrenador es horrible, pero no tenemos otra opción." En cualquier caso, no es una excusa. "Tenemos jugadores capaces de ofrecer un buen desempeño. Cuando no nos queda otra opción, alineamos a los jugadores y nos aseguramos de ganar." A pesar de terminar de trascender en el Real Madrid con la conquista de la novena Champions, la mejor versión de Zidane se vio en Italia durante sus años en la Juventus. Allí ganó el Balón de Oro en 1998. "Cuando llegué a Turín, no estaba jugando muy bien, por eso la prensa y el público no me consideraban a la altura. Lippi me dijo que tenía que jugar con él y perseveré". Aquella Juventus era muy diferente a la actual. Por ello, le preguntaron sobre la posibilidad de que algún día asumiese el banquillo del Allianz Stadium y, aunque acaba de asumir el cargo de la selección francesa, no lo descartó. "¿Por qué no en el futuro?", admitía siempre sonriente.

images.caption: Kylian Mbappé

articles.title: Victoria de oficio de la Real en Estambul y rumbo a cuartos
articles.standfirst: Elimina al Fenerbahçe tras ganar en Turquía y espera al Eintracht o PSV en la siguiente ronda
articles.summary: Elimina al Fenerbahçe tras ganar en Turquía y espera al Eintracht o PSV en la siguiente ronda
articles.body: La Real Sociedad se clasificó para los cuartos de final de la Women’s Europa Cup tras eliminar al Fenerbahçe. El conjunto realista, que ya había ganado (2-0) en Zubieta hace una semana, se impuso este miércoles (0-2) en tierras turcas. La premisa de no especular con el resultado de la ida lo cumplió a rajatabla el conjunto dirigido por Gorka Álvarez, que optó por hacer rotaciones en el once. La Real apenas tardó 49 segundos en anotar y ampliar su ventaja. Un pase filtrado de Cahynova habilitó el centro de Cecilia para Keefe, pero antes de que la chilena contactara con el cuero fue Ndzana quien lo metió en su propia portería en un mal despeje. El combinado otomano intentó reaccionar a base de endurecer los duelos y aumentar el ritmo de juegos para provocar la apertura de espacios. Abideen fue la más incisiva en ataque, probando a Arrula con dos disparos desde las inmediaciones del área. Sin embargo, el que llegaría fue el segundo tanto visitante pasada la media hora de acción. Keefe, que un minuto antes había avisado con un testarazo que logró despejar a córner Munteanu, logró cabecear a la red el posterior saque de esquina botado por Quiles. La primera ocasión de la segunda parte fue para Seker, que remató mordido un centro desde el costado zurdo de Alayont. Luego Abideen estrellaría un balón en el palo tras un mal despeje de Arrula. A la hora de juego, Gorka metió oxígeno con la entrada de Maren, Seelenfreund y Eizagirre. Precisamente Nerea anotó un tercero, a veinte minutos para el final, que no subió al marcador al encontrarse en posición antirreglamentaria tras el pase de Ava. Las locales lo intentaron hasta el final y tuvo dos claras ocasiones en las botas de Uraz, pero primero la zaga y luego Urrola echándose al piso desbarataron el peligro y lograron dejar la portería realista en blanco. La Real Sociedad se cruzará con el ganador de la eliminatoria que enfrenta al Eintracht Frankfurt y PSV, con ventaja (2-0) del equipo alemán en el partido de ida.

images.caption: Las jugadoras de la Real celebran su pase a cuartos. Real Sociedad

articles.title: Dan Lanning Shades Michigan After Kyle Whittingham's Comments About Oregon's NIL Spending
articles.summary: Ahead of Michigan's matchup with Oregon on Saturday, Wolverines' head coach praised his counterpart, Dan Lanning, though added that it "doesn't hurt that you have $50-plus million dollars at your disposal to, in essence, outbid everybody."
articles.body:
Ahead of Michigan's matchup with Oregon on Saturday, Wolverines' head coach praised his counterpart, Dan Lanning, though added that it "doesn't hurt that you have $50-plus million dollars at your disposal to, in essence, outbid everybody."

Lanning, unsurprisingly, responded to those comments on Wednesday.

"I've got nothing to say to Coach Whit other than I think he's an unbelievable coach, and I get it," Lanning told reporters . "They're spending more of their money right now on their coaches that they're letting go, so maybe it makes it hard to sign players. But I know they've signed a couple of guys that we weren't able to compete with what they decided to do, and maybe a lot of that money is tied up for them in another player. I don't know. But Coach Whittingham is an unbelievable coach. He's a Hall of Fame coach. I've got nothing but respect for him."

In Whittingham's full comments, he called Lanning an "outstanding football coach, defensive-minded coach" and noted it wasn't Lanning's fault that he had access to plenty of NIL resources.

"That's a credit to their program and their dedication and desire to win and the support they have. NIL is the name of the game in recruiting these days. It's shifted so much," he said. "It used to be the facilities you had and the tradition and all these other things, and now it's, 'Oh, this is all great, but these guys have a hundred grand more for me.' So that's a little bit of a factor to say the least. But not to take anything away from Dan, because he is an outstanding recruiter."

Neither program has exactly had their desired season in 2026, though the Ducks (6-3) appear to be trending in a better direction after back-to-back ranked wins over Northwestern and Ohio State. Oregon is probably a long shot to reach the College Football Playoff at this point, but should they win out—and perhaps earn a bid to the Big Ten Championship Game—there's at least a chance.

Michigan (5-4), on the other hand, is toast. Since starting 3-0 (which included a controversial win against Western Michigan), the Wolverines have gone just 2-4, largely down to an offense that has been so bad that offensive coordinator Jason Beck was fired after Saturday's 15-6 loss against Michigan State.

And with a brutal stretch to close the season—after Oregon, Michigan faces undefeated UCLA and hated rivals Ohio State—it's possible the Wolverines won't even reach bowl eligibility this season.

articles.title: Pepe Mel evoluciona favorablemente y ya espera una segunda operación
articles.standfirst: Retirada la sedación, reconoce y habla con sus familiares y allegados
articles.summary: Retirada la sedación, reconoce y habla con sus familiares y allegados
articles.body: Las últimas noticias sobre el estado de salud de Pepe Mel invitan a un moderado optimismo. Al técnico madrileño se le ha retirado la sedación y se encuentra despierto, habla y reconoce a sus familiares y allegados, según "El desmarque", a la espera de una segunda intervención. El que fuera jugador y entrenador verdiblanco sufrió hace unos días un accidente cerebrovascular que obligó a ingresarle de urgencia en la Unidad de Cuidados Intensivos del Hospital Universitario Virgen del Rocío. Su estado de salud ha mejorado en las últimas horas, aunque sigue pendiente de una nueva intervención tras el ictus que sufrió el pasado uno de noviembre. La malformación congénita que se le detectó obliga a una nueva operación pero, mientras tanto, las primeras noticias que llegan sobre el técnico madrileño son alentadoras. "La familia de Pepe Mel informa que, durante el día de hoy, una vez retirada la sedación, Pepe ha despertado y ha dado muestras de una buena evolución. Seguirá preparándose para volver a pasar por el quirófano y corregir la malformación congénita que le llevó a sufrir el evento conocido. La familia quiere aprovechar estas líneas, para agradecer las muestras de cariño de todo el mundo del fútbol en general y del Betis y béticos en particular. Seguirá luchando. ¡Gracias a Dios!"

images.caption: Pepe Mel, durante su etapa en el Almería CURRO VALLEJO / MARCA

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo anuncia su primera serie de TV
articles.standfirst: 'Day 1s', que así se llamará, estará ambientada en el mundo de los agentes deportivos
articles.summary: 'Day 1s', que así se llamará, estará ambientada en el mundo de los agentes deportivos
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo ya prepara su vida más allá de los terrenos de juego. El delantero portugués, que acaba de anunciar su adiós definitivo a la selección, desveló a través de sus redes sociales que el rodaje de su primera serie de TV ya está en marcha. 'Day 1s' será el nombre de una serie que estará ambientada en el mundo de los agentes deportivos británicos. El elenco estará encabezado por el actor Damian Lewis, quien dará vida al representante deportivo Stanley Dalton. En la serie aparecerá el propio Cristiano, el exfutbolista francés Thierry Henry y el rapero Dave, protagonista de su primer capítulo. El rodaje ya ha comenzado en Londres pero no se conocen más detalles, ni la fecha de estreno ni la plataforma que emitirá la serie. El trabajo audiovisual está a cargo de UR•Marv Studios, compañía vinculada al deportista luso Cristiano lanzó la exclusiva a través de sus redes sociales, donde publicó el siguiente mensaje: "¡Noticias emocionantes! La producción de mi primer programa de televisión, Day 1s, acaba de comenzar. ¡Habrá más novedades!"

images.caption: Cristiano Ronaldo Instagram

articles.title: SEC's proposed cap policy would penalize big-spending schools $7 million this year
articles.summary: Financial penalties would begin low and gradually increase in a tiered system, but schools that overspend will pay a hefty price.
articles.body:
The SEC may soon begin fining schools that exceed the athlete revenue-share cap.

In a proposed plan the league is socializing with other conferences, the SEC would establish a conference cap policy penalizing schools for spending over the $21.6 million House settlement revenue-share cap, with escalating fines that exceed $10 million for those spending more than $70.5 million on their rosters, according to administrators briefed on the plan.

The SEC's proposal, far different from the Big Ten's cap rules passed last month, would consider some school-affiliated, third-party NIL deals as "institutional pay," implementing terms of the House settlement that have not previously been enforced — with, importantly, the addition of pro sports-like luxury taxes.

Details of the penalty structure, only recently formalized, is new information shared with dozens of administrators over the last several days.

Financial penalties would begin low and gradually increase in a tiered system. Fines begin at less than 1% for those spending below $50.5 million on their rosters, and then increase to 1% for those spending $50.5-60.5 million, then to 3% for those spending $60.5-70.5 million and, finally, to 10% for those spending more than $70.5 million. This means a school could spend $70.5 million on its athletes with a fine of around $7 million.

However, the financial penalties in each tier increase with each new cap year. Next year, for example, the model increases the penalty from 3% to 5% for those spending between $60.5-$70.5 million and from 10% to 15% for those exceeding $70.5 million. The following year, the penalty would reach 20% for the biggest spenders — a tax of roughly around $14-16 million.

It's unclear where the fine money will be distributed and how.

"The headline here is that the new cap would basically be $70 million," said one power league athletic director.

In a concept widely supported by many college leaders, the SEC's proposal may remove the requirement for schools to gain approval from the College Sports Commission's NIL Go clearinghouse for NIL agreements with associated entities redirecting revenue from the athletic department to the roster. These deals likely feature school corporate sponsors, multi-media rights partners and perhaps even apparel brands. They represent a large chunk of submissions in the current system.

This would eliminate what officials say are time-consuming and resource-draining measures to circumvent the existing cap by redirecting revenue to athletes in the form of concocted marketing and endorsement agreements. Many universities are paying as much as 20% to third party entities to "wash money," several power conference leaders contend, in an effort to effectively pass the contracts through the NIL Go clearinghouse.

For now, a retroactive implementation date of Oct. 1 is under discussion for the new fining structure. Third-party NIL deals featuring redirected school revenue that were submitted on or after that date would be considered institutional pay. Only fully independent third-party NIL payments are excluded from the new cap policy, such as authentic marketing and endorsement deals that athletes strike on their own with businesses and brands.

The SEC's proposal would tremendously reduce submissions to the College Sports Commission, the 18-month-old enforcement body charged with policing third-party NIL deals. Though it is conducting more than a dozen active investigations and inquiries into college programs with a staff that now has reached 30 people, the commission has not yet penalized programs for cap circumvention.

Over the last few months, however, the CSC's scrutiny of school-affiliated NIL deals has increased, those with knowledge of the latest submissions say — a move that, perhaps coincidentally, aligns with the development of these conference-cap policies.

The SEC's fining system is meant to close a loophole that schools are using to exceed the cap by redirecting revenue from school-affiliated entities to athletes. But questions still loom on whether the latest proposal completely closes the circumvention loophole.

For example, are all NIL deals — even those from booster-backed collectives — considered as part of the SEC's cap policy? Or can schools still circumvent the system in other ways?

While the proposal originates from the SEC, the four power conferences are expected to attempt to align with similar league cap rules to avoid competitive inequity while adhering to federal collusion laws. Conferences are attempting to create and enforce rules around athlete compensation, player movement and eligibility with hopes that they can avoid antitrust legal challenges that toppled the NCAA's national policies.

The Big Ten last month created new compensation cap rules that will fine schools spending more than $49 million on their rosters in a similarly escalating system. The fining system permits schools to spend the $21.6 million allowed under the House settlement plus $27 million in school-affiliated third-party NIL deals before the penalties begin.

However, the Big Ten's policy features a significant league fine — as much as $25 million — once a school exceeds the $60 million mark.

These conference policies may put leagues at odds with both antitrust laws and with the House settlement itself. In fact, House plaintiff attorneys Jeffrey Kessler and Steve Berman believe the Big Ten's proposal violates settlement terms.

The SEC's plan has its own issues for those lower-resourced programs.

The potential for the biggest spenders to further exploit even the new penalty system strikes fear in those smaller-spending programs, especially those in the Big 12 and ACC. Many officials in those leagues wonder if the loophole is really closed and believe the penalties are not severe enough.

For reference, the MLB's luxury tax is between 20-50%, depending on how many consecutive years that team has exceeded the soft-cap figure.

"Anything north of $50 or $60 million should come with a 1-for-1 tax," said one Big 12 school administrator.

It's unclear if NCAA or College Sports Commission policies would need to change under the SEC's penalty structure. It's also unclear if House settlement terms need amending. To modify settlement terms, the NCAA and the five conferences — the Pac-12 included as it was an original defendant in the House antitrust lawsuit — must agree to changes, along with plaintiffs and their attorneys. It is considered a laborious process that may drag well past January's transfer football portal, when many officials believe conference caps are necessary to slow spending.

The SEC's formalized proposal comes amid what administrators describe as a "chaotic" environment in the industry, where court rulings and state laws have crippled NCAA rules and created a landscape of free player movement, mostly uncapped compensation and even uncertain eligibility standards — which some contend is the fault of college leaders failing to adapt quickly enough.

For some, the solution lies on Capitol Hill, where college leaders have spent years and millions of dollars lobbying lawmakers to pass a congressional bill, the Protect College Sports Act. The legislation attempts to bring order to the unruly environment by limiting athlete movement, establishing eligibility standards and granting the NCAA and College Sports Commission an antitrust exemption to regulate athlete compensation in a way that many believe is unfair.

However, the Act, though overwhelmingly passed by the Senate in striking bipartisan fashion , faces a steep climb in the House of Representatives, which only has five working weeks before a new Congress — and likely a new, more Democrat-friendly bill — arrives in January. The Democrats won back control of both the Senate and House in last week's midterm elections.

Some administrators are frustrated enough to support an employment and collective bargaining model — a concept that, while rife with hurdles, is gaining momentum among stakeholders.

The predicted congressional failure now has conferences returning to what many describe as "Plan B," where leagues create and enforce their own rules.

While on "The Paul Finebaum Show" earlier this week, SEC commissioner Greg Sankey encouraged Congress to pass the legislation to provide regulation around player movement, eligibility and compensation.

If left without a signed bill, conferences "perhaps individually, to the extent they can legally, will have to be involved in addressing those issues directly."

"Some of those are embedded in the Protect College Sports Act," he said. "Some are about conference policies we've had in the past. Some we've emphasized this year. They haven't changed. Others we've introduced as we move forward."

images.caption: SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey is hoping to regulate athlete eligibility and pay, which could be done via a proposed conference salary cap. (Parker S. Freedman via Getty Images)

articles.title: SEC Proposes $70M Salary Cap in New Rumors on Potential CFB Rule Changes, Financial Penalties
articles.summary: The SEC is reportedly one step closer to implementing a pro sports-style salary cap and luxury tax.
articles.body:
The SEC is reportedly one step closer to implementing a pro sports-style salary cap and luxury tax.

Per Yahoo Sports' Ross Dellenger , the conference proposed a new cap policy that would penalize schools that spent over the $21.6 million House settlement revenue-share cap.

The proposal features escalating fines of more than $10 million for schools that spent more than $70.5 million on their rosters.

According to Dellenger, some third-party NIL deals that are school-affiliated would be considered "institutional pay" under the new proposal, which would implement previously unenforced terms of the House settlement.

"The headline here is that the new cap would basically be $70 million," one power conference athletic director told Dellenger.

The SEC shared details of the penalty structure with "dozens of administrators" this week. According to Dellenger, the structure is as follows:

Less than 1 percent for schools spending below $50.5 million

1 percent for schools spending $50.5 to $60.5

3 percent for schools spending $60.5 to $70.5

10 percent for schools spending more than $70.5 million

The financial penalties for each tier would also increase in each new cap year. Dellenger noted, however, that it remains unclear where the fine money will be distributed.

The proposal comes two weeks after the Big Ten announced that it would implement a $49 million NIL spending cap for all of its schools. Unlike the SEC's proposal, the one from the Big Ten is designed to mirror the one proposed in the Protect College Sports Act, which is currently awaiting a vote in the House of Representatives.

The Big Ten's policy caps revenue-sharing at $21.6 million and third-party NIL spending at $27.5 million.

The SEC's proposed cap system has a retroactive implementation date of Oct. 1, according to Dellenger.

articles.title: Colin Cowherd thinks Curt Cignetti story has been ‘overplayed’ as Indiana falls in CFP rankings
articles.summary: Colin Cowherd devoted a segment of Wednesday’s “The Herd with Colin Cowherd” on FS1 to the Indiana Hoosiers, a day after the College Football Playoff selecti...
articles.body:
Colin Cowherd devoted a segment of Wednesday's "The Herd with Colin Cowherd" on FS1 to the Indiana Hoosiers, a day after the College Football Playoff selection committee dropped them from No. 4 to No. 9 during their bye week. Indiana hosts the USC Trojans on Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET, and Curt Cignetti has yet to say who will start at quarterback.

"I will say, and I say this as somebody who works for a company that has their arms around the Big Ten, I think the Curt Cignetti story is awesome. I think it's been a little overplayed. I thought he got about 90% of the credit for their national championship, and I think Mendoza deserved at least half of it. Under Cignetti, the offense is a BB gun without Mendoza. They schedule a weak out of conference, but his record is otherworldly. It's 35 and 3, and he took over a bad program. He's a really, really good coach, but he's not Saban. Saban, both sides of the ball. Players became irrelevant at Alabama. Offense, defense, you couldn't separate them. They were great at both. That's not what Indiana is. Indiana, he sets a very high floor foundationally and culturally. Mendoza was the ceiling." Cowherd said.

Cignetti coached receivers and ran recruiting on Saban's staff at the Alabama Crimson Tide from 2007 to 2010, so Cowherd measured him against the man he once worked for.

The 35-3 mark covers an 11-2 first season, last year's 16-0 title run and this season's 8-1 start, with the North Texas Mean Green, Howard Bison and Western Kentucky Hilltoppers making up this year's nonconference schedule.

"I'll give you an example of this. If you look at Indiana against ranked opponents under Curt Cignetti, when Mendoza played, they averaged 38 a game and win by three touchdowns. Without Mendoza, including this year, they're 0-3 and they score 15 points. They're over double the offense with Fernando Mendoza, now a Raider, than they are without it. Cignetti is super conservative. Nick Saban was not offensively. Cignetti's really conservative. He's not the recruiter of Saban. I think he's a very, very good coach, but he got an incredible amount of the love on that 16-0 team that could have easily lost five games if Mendoza wasn't the quarterback." Cowherd said.

Mendoza went 6-0 against AP top-10 opponents last season, and Indiana scored 227 points in those six games, just under 38 per game. Indiana scored 47 points combined in its three losses under Cignetti: 38-15 at the Ohio State Buckeyes and 27-17 at the Notre Dame Fighting Irish in the playoff's first round in 2024, then 19-15 at home against Ohio State last month. Last season also produced one-score wins over the Iowa Hawkeyes, Penn State Nittany Lions, Ohio State and Miami Hurricanes, which, of course, were the close calls behind Cowherd's five-loss point.

Does Cowherd's ranked-opponent split prove the Mendoza point?

Two of the three losses came in 2024, Cignetti's first season after taking over in November 2023, with Ohio Bobcats transfer Kurtis Rourke at quarterback. The third came in the game where Josh Hoover hurt his right shoulder. The "without Mendoza" column holds a first-year rebuild and an injured quarterback, which makes it as much a measure of roster age and health as of one player.

Hoover, the TCU Horned Frogs transfer brought in to replace Mendoza, went his first seven games without an interception and threw four touchdown passes in both the North Texas win and the 47-15 rout of the Rutgers Scarlet Knights. He left the Ohio State game briefly after the injury and came back. Across the two games since, he has completed 16 of 37 passes, and Cignetti pulled him at halftime against the Minnesota Golden Gophers on Oct. 31 after a hit on an interception return. Grant Wilson, a seventh-year backup, went 9 of 17 for 156 yards in relief and threw the winning touchdown in overtime.

"Our defense the last four or five games has been really solid. Offensively, we're not producing like we had the previous two years. Our consistency is not there right now," Cignetti said on his weekly radio show during the bye week.

Indiana has not reached 21 points in regulation in any of its last four games, and it won three of them while allowing 58 points in total.

"I'm not saying Mendoza is going to be Peyton Manning. Nor am I saying Cignetti is not an excellent coach. I think he's a really good coach, but I would not be shocked if they lost to USC. I really wouldn't. They're both off a bye. I wouldn't be shocked. I think USC's got much more firepower offensively. Oh, Indiana moved down five spots while they were on a bye? Is that what people were talking about? I don't spend a lot of time on where these are ranked. I think Georgia, Notre Dame, Miami are the only three teams that can win a national championship." Cowherd said.

USC sits No. 18 in the committee's rankings at 7-2. A healthy Hoover against that team would give Cowherd's ceiling argument its fairest test, and a stalled offense with him at full strength would hand the FS1 host his best evidence yet.

Cignetti has kept the starting job open since Hoover's exit against Minnesota.

articles.title: ‘No hot seat’: Oklahoma backs Brent Venables, and his $51.67 million buyout explains why
articles.summary: The University of Oklahoma Board of Regents met in Norman on Wednesday morning, and chair Rick Nagel used the session to address a subject the board usually...
articles.body:
The University of Oklahoma Board of Regents met in Norman on Wednesday morning, and chair Rick Nagel used the session to address a subject the board usually leaves to the athletic department.

The Oklahoma Sooners are 5-4 in Brent Venables' fifth season, with the No. 19 Ole Miss Rebels visiting Norman on Saturday. Oklahoma has never beaten Ole Miss, and the Rebels won in Norman last season. Oklahoma then hosts the Texas A&M Aggies on Nov. 21 and closes the regular season at the Missouri Tigers on Nov. 28.

"The board doesn't typically comment much on what's going on in the athletic department. That's maybe a smart thing. But I want to say this … our head coach, Brent Venables, is not on the hot seat. There is no hot seat. We just extended his contract," Nagel said, as reported by Joe Mussatto of The Oklahoman.

That extension, agreed to in August and approved by the regents in September, runs six years and $63 million through Jan. 31, 2032. Venables is making $10 million this season, with $200,000 raises each year after, and contract documents put his buyout at $51.67 million if Oklahoma moves on from him on Dec. 1. SoonerScoop's George Stoia calculated that the same decision would have cost roughly $26.2 million without the extension.

The deal also added incentives tied to College Football Playoff success. The board doubled the price of a coaching change in the summer, weeks before a season that has looked a lot like Venables' other even-numbered years.

How Venables' up-and-down tenure reached this point

Venables is 37-24 at Oklahoma and 0-4 in bowl and playoff games. His first four seasons alternated between 6-7 finishes in 2022 and 2024 and 10-3 finishes in 2023 and 2025, and the most recent of those 10-win teams lost in the first round of the College Football Playoff.

Oklahoma has followed the same rhythm week to week this fall. The Sooners beat the No. 1 Texas Longhorns 27-24 on Oct. 10 on a field goal as time expired, then lost 21-13 at home to the Kentucky Wildcats on Oct. 17. A 42-25 home loss to the South Carolina Gamecocks on Oct. 31 was followed by Venables firing offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle, and the Sooners responded with a 23-7 win at the Florida Gators last Saturday that included a 20-play touchdown drive.

"A thing of beauty. Fabulous in every way," Venables said of that drive after the game.

The swings cut both ways for the board. Oklahoma has wins over Texas and at Florida, and it also has home losses to Kentucky and South Carolina. A program that can beat the top-ranked team in the country in October and lose at home to Kentucky the next week gives an administration reasons to believe in the coach and reasons to doubt him, sometimes inside the same month.

Nagel answered the hot-seat question by pointing to the contract, and that is the most direct explanation on the table. A board that committed $63 million in August and raised the cost of a firing to $51.67 million made its decision on Venables before the season started, and Wednesday's statement put that decision on the record before Ole Miss arrives in Norman.

Whatever the final three games produce, the Sooners' leadership has already told the public what it is willing to pay to find out.

articles.title: Travis Etienne Jr.'s Practice Return Creates Murky Fantasy Football Situation in the New Orleans Saints' Backfield
articles.summary: Travis Etienne has returned to practice for the New Orleans Saints. Breakdown of his fantasy football value and the ripple effect on Alvin Kamara and Audric...
articles.body:
The Saints Backfield Shuffle: What Travis Etienne's Impending Return Means for Fantasy Football Managers

The New Orleans Saints backfield is about to get much more crowded. Head coach Kellen Moore delivered a big update for fantasy managers, announcing that running back Travis Etienne Jr. has officially returned to practice. Etienne has been sidelined since suffering a hamstring injury in Week 3 against the Las Vegas Raiders, sending him to injured reserve and forcing fantasy managers to pivot.

Now, with the Saints opening his 21-day practice window, the team will "see how the week plays out" before determining if he is ready to suit up for a crucial divisional clash. While Etienne's return is a welcome boost for a New Orleans offense looking to secure the NFC South crown, it introduces a major headache for fantasy managers holding shares of Alvin Kamara and breakout waiver wire darling Audric Estime.

Let's try to make heads and tails of the fantasy football ripple effects of this news.

Evaluating Travis Etienne's Fantasy Ceiling

Before his multi-week absence, Etienne had accumulated 128 rushing yards on 30 carries with 51 receiving yards through three games. Expectations were high when he signed a marquee multi-year deal with the Saints in free agency, and his dual-threat skill set makes him an explosive centerpiece when healthy.

However, managers should temper expectations for his immediate return. Hamstring injuries are notoriously tricky for running backs, and Kellen Moore's cautious tone suggests they may ease him back into the rotation (if he even plays against the Carolina Panthers this week).

Once fully integrated, Etienne projects as an RB2 with week-winning capabilities, particularly in PPR formats due to his pass-catching ability. But his immediate Week 10 outlook carries some volatility as he knocks off the rust.

The Downward Spiral for Alvin Kamara and Audric Estime

Etienne's impending return is bad news for fantasy managers planning on relying on Alvin Kamara or Audric Estime down the stretch. During Etienne's lengthy five-game absence, the Saints' backfield morphed into a shifting puzzle. Alvin Kamara has continued to command a steady role, but his efficiency and volume have fluctuated. An active Etienne directly eats into his touches, explosive play opportunities, and red-zone looks that anchor Kamara's weekly floor. While Kamara's skill set keeps him relevant, his path to anything more than risky flex numbers narrows significantly once Etienne assumes his starting workload.

Audric Estime is even more vulnerable. He capitalized on the depleted depth chart to carve out an expanded role and became a popular waiver-wire pickup this week, but a healthy Etienne completely caps Estime's fantasy football utility. Without an outright injury ahead of him on the depth chart, Estime projects to slide back into a game-script-dependent rotational role, making him difficult to trust in most leagues.

If you roster Travis Etienne, hold tight and make sure he is stashed safely in your active or IR spot as he nears a game-day designation. If you are relying on Alvin Kamara, prepare for a hit to his weekly ceiling as touches are redistributed. As for Audric Estime managers, it might be time to treat him strictly as a high-end handcuff. The Saints are still very much in the NFC South playoff hunt, and how this three-way backfield shakes out as part of their playoff push will dictate fantasy championships across the board.

articles.title: Lions LG Christian Mahogany on benching: 'I have to grow up'
articles.summary: Detroit Lions LG Christian Mahogany spoke to reporters Wednesday for the first time since he was benched during a victory over the Miami Dolphins.
articles.body:
Christian Mahogany appeared full of remorse and regret.

"It sucks what happened," he said in one breath.

"I have to grow up, and I have to stop breaking team rules," he added in another.

Mahogany made those remarks Wednesday, Nov. 11, as he met with reporters for the first time since he was benched for disciplinary reasons during the Detroit Lions' 19-9 victory over the Miami Dolphins last weekend .

The third-year left guard said he apologized to his teammates and coaches but didn't reveal what led to his punishment.

He did vow, however, that it "won't ever happen again."

"You just got to eat it on the chin," Mahogany said. "I'm not going to sulk."

Before the Lions ' walkthrough practice Wednesday, head coach Dan Campbell said Mahogany would resume work with the first team.

Second-year lineman Miles Frazier, who made his first career start in place of Mahogany on Sunday, struggled while playing all 59 offensive snaps at left guard against the Dolphins .

No Lions lineman graded out worse than Frazier, according to Pro Football Focus.

"It sucked not being out there," said Mahogany, who was actually on the field for each of Jake Bates' four made field goals as well as his lone point-after attempt. "I let my teammates down, and I don't want to do that. I did. That's on me."

Center Juice Scruggs said he was appreciative Mahogany took accountability and was earnest about his desire to make amends.

"The biggest thing is you've got to learn from it," Scruggs told the Free Press. "Don't make the same mistake twice. Just learn from it, move on, and grow as a player and a person. We've all got his back. We know the type of guy he is. We all know the type of teammate he is. We're just going to move forward from it."

"I can't let last week affect me," he said.

Prior to his benching, Mahogany had been enjoying his best season as a pro. Known as a strong blocker, he has become much sturdier in pass protection. A year after he surrendered a team-high six sacks , he has yet to allow one in 2026, according to PFF.

A lineup with Mahogany is stronger than one without him.

But when the week began, Campbell was noncommittal about whether Mahogany would be back in his post between Scruggs and left tackle Penei Sewell this Sunday for the Lions' showdown with the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany.

"The ball is in his court," Campbell said Monday.

Two days later, the Lions coach appeared to indicate Mahogany was on the verge of regaining his starting spot, noting that the plan was for him to practice with the top unit Wednesday.

"I'm on to New England," Mahogany said. "I'm ready to go."

Quarterback Jared Goff (chest) appeared on the team's injury report Wednesday. He was limited during the team's walkthrough practice, along with receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib) and safeties Kerby Joseph (knee) and Brian Branch (hip).

Meanwhile, center Cade Mays (ankle) and cornerback D.J. Reed (hip), who were sidelined Sunday, did not practice and Campbell told reporters that they are unlikely to return to action against the Patriots . Backup running back Sione Vaki (ankle) also sat out Wednesday. Edge defender DJ Wonnum (concussion) and kick returner Jacob Saylors (neck/hamstring) were full participants.

articles.title: Liverpool’s Rio Ngumoha says Harry Kane winning the Ballon d’Or encouraging for English footballl
articles.summary: Ngumoha feels Kane’s Ballon d’Or win is huge for English football
articles.body:
Harry Kane winning the Ballon d'Or at the end of last month in London was a bit of poetic justice that the award itself has been clamoring for after years of past awards and voting breakdowns laden with controversy. This time around, it was incredibly hard to argue against the 73 goals and 8 assists Kane tallied for Bayern Munich and England from a total of only 65 matches — an unprecedented feat. Real Madrid and France's Kylian Mbappé and Barcelona and Spain's Lamine Yamal put up valiant efforts in trying to beat Kane to the crown with incredible seasons for club and country of their own, but it wasn't enough to edge out the England skipper.

For now, Kane is switching gears from Bayern to England coming off matches where he hasn't scored since Bayern's 2-2 draw with Arsenal in the Champions League on October 21st, but he's tallied five assists from that same stretch of matches across all competitions. He's temporarily turned provider for the German Rekordmeister and he set a record for having reached 8 Bundesliga assists after only 9 match weeks. That's the quickest any player has ever reached that tally at this point of the season.

England have a pair of UEFA Nations League matches against Croatia and Spain coming up, with hopes of eclipsing Spain at the top spot of the Nations League group.

In the Three Lions' squad, Thomas Tuchel has included Liverpool's Rio Ngumoha, who's in a good spell of form for Andoni Iraola's side and will be looking to gain more experience for England's senior team having made his competitive debut in the 2-0 win over Czechia at the end of September. Ahead of the pair of matches against Croatia and Spain, the Liverpool youngster raved about how big it is for English football that Kane won the Ballon d'Or. After all, he's the first England player to have won the award since Michael Owen did so back in 2001.

"Harry Kane winning the Ballon d'Or is definitely a big, big thing, being known as the best player in the world. It's also helped English football now because everyone's seen one of us win the Ballon d'Or, it is definitely encouraging many more people to wanting to be known as the best player in the world. For me, I would like to achieve it and I think I can do it," Ngumoha told the Liverpool Echo (via @iMiaSanMia ).

Kane can certainly take added delight with the motivation his achievements are giving young English players, and Ngumoha is on a trajectory at Liverpool that could very well turn him into a world-class player. He's competing for minutes with the likes of Cody Gakpo, Bradley Barcola, Victor Muñoz, and Florian Wirtz, which is a tall order, but he's been making the most of the opportunities Iraola has been giving him. The Spaniard is gaining a level of trust in the winger and rewarding him with minutes and occasional starts as he rotates the squad from competition to competition.
